text:
Alex: Quick Q — noticed weirdness with stop + max_tokens + temperature/top_p. If I send:

```json
{
  "model": "r-infer-1",
  "prompt": "Write a short haiku about caches",
  "max_tokens": 16,
  "stop": ["\n\n"],
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "top_p": 1.0,
  "logprobs": 5,
  "stream": false
}
```

I get output that looks trimmed and yet the last returned token still has a non-null logprob (so we scored something that later got trimmed). Is that expected by contract? Also, when I try `stream=true` I don't get logprobs at all — is that intentional or a bug?

Priya: For the hosted API the intended contract is: stop sequences are post-processing and the final `text` should exclude the stop. `logprobs` should reflect tokens actually scored by the model. That said, we previously had an off-by-one where a token that matched the stop was still included in scoring metadata. Can you paste the exact response you got? :thinking: 

Alex: Pasting anonymized response (trimmed):

```
{"text":"Autumn cache warms the...","tokens":["Autumn"," cache"," warms"," the","..."],"logprobs":[-1.2,-0.8,-0.9,-2.3,null]}
```

See last token logprob `null` but the one before it has a value even though the stop should have removed that token.

Sam: This rings a bell — runtime bug where `max_tokens` was applied before stop-matching in some execution paths (quantized kernels + cached KV). Result: we sometimes score a token that later gets trimmed. Filed INF-412 for this exact symptom. Short-term workaround: bump `max_tokens` by 1-2 or put a more specific `stop` token boundary.

Maria: I'll add a unit test to the serving-runtime tests that asserts: if stop matches, `text` excludes stop and `logprobs` correspond to remaining tokens. @Sam can you add the INF-412 case to the regression harness and add a note for streaming?

Sam: Yep, adding to harness. Also note on temp/top_p: when `temperature=0` we treat as greedy (temp override) and ignore stochastic sampling — i.e., `top_p` has no effect. That should be explicit in the API contract. I saw a bug where `temperature` was 0 but `top_p` still caused nucleus sampling in a fallback path. Will include that in the PR.

Alex: Great. Can someone draft the exact sentence we should put in the docs so I can paste? Want to avoid ambiguous language.

Priya: Draft: 
- "Stop sequences are applied as post-processing and are removed from the `text` field returned by the API."
- "`logprobs` are provided only for tokens that were actually scored; tokens removed by stop-trimming are not guaranteed to have corresponding logprob entries."
- "When `stream=true`, per-token `logprobs` may be omitted depending on chunk boundaries; streaming does not guarantee full `logprobs` metadata."
- "If `max_tokens` would cause truncation before a stop match, truncation takes precedence (this is a known behavior we are evaluating to change)."
- "`temperature=0` implies greedy decoding; `top_p`/`top_k` are ignored in that mode."

Maria: That looks good. I'll paste into the docs PR and link INF-412. Also adding a tiny e2e test to the canary suite.

Sam: Quick note — please include an example curl test we can run for sanity: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"r-infer-1","prompt":"x","max_tokens":2,"stop":["\n"],"logprobs":5}'
```

Alex: Thanks all. @Maria @Sam please ping when PRs ready and I'll do a quick review. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: INF-412 test added to nightly pipeline, will run on next deploy.
